prompt: A quilt block is a square $8$ inches on each side. A ribbon is sewn along one diagonal. How long is the ribbon, in inches, rounded to the nearest tenth?
hint: A diagonal cuts the square into two $45^\circ$-$45^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangles.

hints.text: A diagonal cuts the square into two $45^\circ$-$45^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangles.
In a $45$-$45$-$90$ triangle the hypotenuse is leg $\times \sqrt{2}$, so the diagonal is $8\sqrt{2}$.

explanation: The diagonal of a square makes two isosceles right triangles with legs $8$ and $8$.
The $45$-$45$-$90$ shortcut gives hypotenuse $= 8\sqrt{2}$ (the Pythagorean theorem agrees: $\sqrt{64 + 64} = \sqrt{128}$).

alternativeExplanations.title: Estimate first, then trust it
steps: The diagonal must be longer than $8$ but shorter than $8 + 8 = 16$, so somewhere in the low teens.
$\sqrt{2} \approx 1.4$, so about $8(1.4) = 11.2$ — right in that window, which confirms $11.3$ is sensible.
